subproblems.title: Complement of a Gauss-Green pair: (μ, −ν) represents U ∖ E (parent Part 1a, erratum E5)
subproblems.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N open, E ⊆ ℝ^N Lebesgue null-measurable, μ a Borel measure on ℝ^N and ν : ℝ^N → ℝ^N such that (μ, ν) is a Gauss-Green pair for (U, E) (IsGaussGreenPair U E μ ν: μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = 0; μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U; ν is μ-a.e. strongly measurable; |ν| = 1 μ-a.e.; ∫_{E∩U} div g dL^N = −∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ for every C¹ compactly supported g : ℝ^N → ℝ^N with tsupport g ⊆ U). Then (μ, −ν) is a Gauss-Green pair for (U, U ∖ E), i.e. IsGaussGreenPair U (U ∖ E) μ (−ν).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (U E : Set (Rn N)) (μ : Measure (Rn N)) (ν : Rn N → Rn N), IsOpen U → NullMeasurableSet E volume → IsGaussGreenPair U E μ ν → IsGaussGreenPair U (U \ E) μ (-ν)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof Part 1a (erratum E5): Simon, Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 4.3, chapter-03.txt line 729 ("Repeating the same argument with U ∖ E in place of E"), which tacitly uses that (μ_E, −ν) represents Dχ_{U∖E} in U.

Notation. L^N = volume; div g = Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanDivergence g = trace(Dg) (0 where g is not differentiable). For a C¹ field g, div g is continuous.

Proof. Fix N, U, E, μ, ν with IsGaussGreenPair U E μ ν, i.e. (a) μ(Uᶜ) = 0, (b) μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, (c) ν is AEStronglyMeasurable for μ, (d) ‖ν(y)‖ = 1 for μ-a.e. y, (e) ∫_{E∩U} div g dL^N = −∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ for every C¹ g with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ U. We verify the five clauses of IsGaussGreenPair U (U ∖ E) μ (−ν).

1. Clauses (a) and (b) involve neither the set nor the normal, so they hold verbatim.

2. Clause (c): −ν = (y ↦ −ν(y)) is AEStronglyMeasurable for μ as the negation of an AEStronglyMeasurable function. Clause (d): ‖(−ν)(y)‖ = ‖ν(y)‖ = 1 for μ-a.e. y.

3. Fix g : ℝ^N → ℝ^N, C¹, with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ U. Dg vanishes on the open set ℝ^N ∖ tsupport g, so div g is continuous and vanishes outside tsupport g (SimonGMT support_euclideanDivergence_subset); hence div g is Lebesgue integrable.

4. Claim: ∫_{ℝ^N} div g dL^N = 0. With respect to the standard orthonormal basis (e_i), div g = Σ_i ∂_i g_i, where g_i := ⟨e_i, g⟩ is a C¹ compactly supported real function and ∂_i g_i(y) = Dg_i(y)e_i (SimonGMT euclideanDivergence_eq_sum_inner). Fix i. For t ≠ 0, translation invariance of L^N gives ∫ (g_i(y + te_i) − g_i(y))/t dy = 0. For 0 < |t| ≤ 1 these difference quotients are bounded by sup|Dg_i| (mean value theorem) and vanish outside the compact set tsupport g + B̄_1(0); they converge pointwise to ∂_i g_i(y) as t → 0. Dominated convergence gives ∫ ∂_i g_i dL^N = 0; summing over i proves the claim.

5. Since div g = 0 outside tsupport g ⊆ U, ∫_U div g dL^N = ∫_{ℝ^N} div g dL^N = 0.

6. E ∩ U and U ∖ E are disjoint L^N-null-measurable sets (E null-measurable, U open) with union U, and (U ∖ E) ∩ U = U ∖ E. By additivity of the integral of the integrable function div g and clause (e) for (U, E):
 ∫_{(U∖E)∩U} div g = ∫_U div g − ∫_{E∩U} div g = 0 − (−∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ) = ∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ.

7. Pointwise ⟨g(y), (−ν)(y)⟩ = −⟨g(y), ν(y)⟩, so ∫⟨g, −ν⟩ dμ = −∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ (the Bochner integral commutes with negation whether or not the integrand is integrable). Hence ∫_{(U∖E)∩U} div g = −∫⟨g, −ν⟩ dμ, which is clause (e) for (U, U ∖ E, μ, −ν).

8. All five clauses hold, so IsGaussGreenPair U (U ∖ E) μ (−ν). ∎
proof_key_steps: μ(Uᶜ) = 0 and finiteness on compact subsets of U are unchanged; −ν is μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |−ν| = 1 μ-a.e.
For C¹ compactly supported g: div g is integrable, vanishes off tsupport g ⊆ U, and ∫_{ℝ^N} div g = 0 (difference quotients, translation invariance, dominated convergence), so ∫_U div g = 0.
∫_{U∖E} div g = ∫_U div g − ∫_{E∩U} div g = ∫⟨g, ν⟩dμ = −∫⟨g, −ν⟩dμ by (GG) for (U, E).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof Part 1b (with R = identity); Simon, Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 4.3, display (8), chapter-03.txt lines 668-672 ("write ζ_k(x) = ζ(ρ_k⁻¹x) and change variable x → ρ_k x; then ∫_{ρ_k⁻¹E} D_iζ = ρ_k^{−n} ∫_E D_iζ_k = ... (by 4.1)").

Notation. L^N = volume; div g = euclideanDivergence g = trace(Dg). IsGaussGreenPair U E μ ν includes (GG): ∫_{E∩U} div h dL^N = −∫⟨h, ν⟩ dμ for every C¹ h with compact support and tsupport h ⊆ U.

Proof. Fix the data. η(y) = r⁻¹(y − x) is an affine homeomorphism of ℝ^N with inverse η⁻¹(z) = x + rz and constant derivative Dη = r⁻¹·id.

1. Put h := g ∘ η. Then h is C¹ (a C¹ map composed with an affine map). Since η is a homeomorphism, tsupport h = η⁻¹(tsupport g), which is compact (the image of the compact set tsupport g under the continuous map η⁻¹); so h has compact support. As η is injective, tsupport h ⊆ η⁻¹(η(U)) = U.

2. By the chain rule Dh(y) = Dg(η(y)) ∘ (r⁻¹ id) = r⁻¹ Dg(η(y)); taking traces, div h(y) = r⁻¹ (div g)(η(y)) for every y.

3. ⟨h(y), ν(y)⟩ = ⟨g(η(y)), ν(y)⟩ for every y.

4. (GG) for (U, E) applied to h gives ∫_{E∩U} r⁻¹ (div g)(η(y)) dy = −∫⟨g(η(y)), ν(y)⟩ dμ(y).

5. Change of variables. For Borel B, L^N(η⁻¹(B)) = L^N(x + rB) = r^N L^N(B) (translation invariance and scaling of Lebesgue measure; Mathlib Measure.addHaar_smul, Measure.addHaar_image_homothety). Hence the image measure of L^N under η is r^N L^N, and for every null-measurable A and every bounded Borel f with compact support, ∫_A f(η(y)) dy = r^N ∫_{η(A)} f(z) dz. With A := E ∩ U (null-measurable) and f := div g (continuous with compact support):
 ∫_{E∩U} r⁻¹(div g)(η(y)) dy = r^{N−1} ∫_{η(E∩U)} div g = rⁿ ∫_{η(E) ∩ η(U)} div g,
 because η is injective, so η(E ∩ U) = η(E) ∩ η(U).

6. div g vanishes outside tsupport g ⊆ η(U), hence ∫_{η(E)∩η(U)} div g = ∫_{η(E)} div g.

7. Steps 4-6 give rⁿ ∫_{η(E)} div g dL^N = −∫⟨g(η(y)), ν(y)⟩ dμ(y). Dividing by rⁿ > 0: ∫_{η(E)} div g dL^N = −(rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫⟨g(η(y)), ν(y)⟩ dμ(y). ∎
proof_key_steps: h := g ∘ η_{x,r} is C¹ with compact support and tsupport h = η⁻¹(tsupport g) ⊆ U.
div h = r⁻¹(div g)∘η and ⟨h, ν⟩ = ⟨g∘η, ν⟩; apply (GG) for (U, E) to h.
Change of variables z = η(y) (η pushes L^N to r^N L^N): ∫_{E∩U} (div g)∘η = r^N ∫_{η(E)∩η(U)} div g; div g vanishes off η(U); divide by rⁿ.

Let x ∈ ∂*E := reducedBoundary U μ ν (x ∈ U and normalAverage μ ν x ρ = μ(B_ρ(x)).toReal⁻¹ • ∫_{B_ρ(x)} ν dμ converges as ρ ↓ 0 to a unit vector) and e := ν_E(x) := reducedNormal μ ν x (that limit). subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof Parts 1c, 2 and 3e: Simon, Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 4.3, (1)-(6) (chapter-03.txt lines 607-652) and the Sobolev step leading to (10), (11) (lines 689-733), with erratum E5 (the complement is handled with the pair (μ, −ν) of sibling compl_pair) and erratum E6 (for n = 0 the Sobolev inequality is replaced by its one-dimensional L^∞ form). Here the point x and the unit vector e = ν_E(x) are kept general instead of normalizing to x = 0, e = e_N (parent Part 1b); the argument is unchanged.

Notation. N := n + 1; L^N = volume; B_ρ := B_ρ(x) (open), B̄_ρ := closed ball; ω_N := L^N(B_1(0)); m(ρ) := μ(B_ρ); V(ρ) := L^N(E ∩ B_ρ) and V_c(ρ) := L^N(B_ρ ∖ E) (finite and non-decreasing in ρ); for a Lipschitz ζ, ∇ζ is its a.e. gradient (Rademacher); div g = euclideanDivergence g; φ_σ (σ > 0) is a standard mollifier (C^∞, ≥ 0, even, ∫φ_σ = 1, spt φ_σ ⊆ B̄_σ(0)). IsGaussGreenPair U E μ ν gives (a) μ(Uᶜ) = 0, (b) μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, (c) ν μ-a.e. strongly measurable, (d) |ν| = 1 μ-a.e., (e) (GG) ∫_{E∩U} div g = −∫⟨g, ν⟩ dμ for C¹ g with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ U. By sibling compl_pair, (μ, −ν) is a Gauss-Green pair for (U, U ∖ E).

Step 0 (the unit vector e). Since x ∈ ∂*E, x ∈ U and there is v with |v| = 1 and normalAverage(x, ρ) → v as ρ ↓ 0. The filter 𝓝[>]0 on ℝ is non-trivial and ℝ^N is Hausdorff, so e = reducedNormal μ ν x = limUnder (𝓝[>]0) (normalAverage μ ν x) = v; thus |e| = 1.

Step 1 (radius ρ₀ and positivity; parent 1c). Choose ρ₀ > 0 with B̄_{ρ₀} ⊆ U. For 0 < ρ ≤ ρ₀, m(ρ) ≤ μ(B̄_{ρ₀}) < ∞ by (b). For every ρ > 0, m(ρ) > 0: otherwise m(ρ') = 0 for all ρ' ∈ (0, ρ], hence ∫_{B_{ρ'}} ν dμ = 0 and normalAverage(x, ρ') = 0 for those ρ', so the limit e would be 0, contradicting |e| = 1.

Step 2 (Simon (1) and (2)). For 0 < ρ ≤ ρ₀, ν is μ-integrable on B_ρ (|ν| ≤ 1 a.e., finite measure), normalAverage(x, ρ) = m(ρ)⁻¹ ∫_{B_ρ} ν dμ, and
 a(ρ) := ⟨normalAverage(x, ρ), e⟩ = m(ρ)⁻¹ ∫_{B_ρ} ⟨ν, e⟩ dμ → ⟨e, e⟩ = 1 as ρ ↓ 0; also a(ρ) ≤ 1.
Since |ν| = |e| = 1 μ-a.e., |ν − e|² = 2(1 − ⟨ν, e⟩) μ-a.e., and by the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality
 (2') ∫_{B_ρ} |ν − e| dμ ≤ m(ρ)^{1/2} (∫_{B_ρ} |ν − e|² dμ)^{1/2} = m(ρ) (2(1 − a(ρ)))^{1/2}.

Step 3 (Gauss-Green for Lipschitz fields; Simon (3)). Claim: (GG) holds for every Lipschitz g : ℝ^N → ℝ^N with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ U, for the pair (U, E, μ, ν) and for the pair (U, U ∖ E, μ, −ν). Proof: choose σ₀ > 0 with K' := {y : dist(y, tsupport g) ≤ σ₀} ⊆ U (K' is compact; tsupport g is a compact subset of the open set U), and put g_σ := φ_σ * g. For σ < σ₀, g_σ is C^∞ with tsupport g_σ ⊆ K' ⊆ U, so (GG) holds for g_σ. As σ → 0, g_σ → g uniformly (g is uniformly continuous). If g is L-Lipschitz, g is differentiable a.e. with |Dg| ≤ L, and for each direction w the difference quotients (g(· + tw) − g)/t are bounded by L|w| and converge a.e. to Dg(·)w; convolving with φ_σ and using dominated convergence, D g_σ(·)w = φ_σ * (Dg(·)w). Hence div g_σ = φ_σ * div g, |div g_σ| ≤ NL, and div g_σ → div g a.e. as σ → 0 (Lebesgue differentiation theorem). All these functions vanish off K', L^N(K') < ∞, μ(K') < ∞ and |⟨g_σ, ν⟩| ≤ sup|g| μ-a.e.; dominated convergence on both sides of (GG) for g_σ gives (GG) for g.
 Consequences. Let ζ : ℝ^N → ℝ be Lipschitz with compact support and tsupport ζ ⊆ U and let |w| = 1. Applying the claim to g := ζw (div g = ⟨∇ζ, w⟩ a.e., ⟨g, ν⟩ = ζ⟨w, ν⟩) and using ∇ζ = 0 a.e. outside U:
 (3) ∫ ζ⟨ν, w⟩ dμ = −∫_E ⟨∇ζ, w⟩ dL^N ≤ ∫_E |∇ζ| dL^N;
and applying it to the pair (μ, −ν) for (U, U ∖ E) with the vector −w:
 (3c) ∫ ζ⟨ν, w⟩ dμ = ∫ ζ⟨−ν, −w⟩ dμ = −∫_{U∖E} ⟨∇ζ, −w⟩ dL^N ≤ ∫_{U∖E} |∇ζ| dL^N.

Step 4 (Simon (4), (5)). V and V_c are non-decreasing, hence differentiable at a.e. ρ (Lebesgue; Mathlib Monotone.ae_differentiableAt). Fix ρ ∈ (0, ρ₀) at which V and V_c are differentiable. For k ∈ ℕ with 1/k < ρ let ζ_k(y) := φ_k(|y − x|), where φ_k(t) = 1 for t ≤ ρ − 1/k, φ_k(t) = k(ρ − t) for ρ − 1/k ≤ t ≤ ρ, φ_k(t) = 0 for t ≥ ρ. Then ζ_k is k-Lipschitz, 0 ≤ ζ_k ≤ 1, tsupport ζ_k = B̄_ρ ⊆ U, ζ_k is non-decreasing in k and ζ_k → 1_{B_ρ} pointwise. On the open annulus A_k := {ρ − 1/k < |y − x| < ρ}, ∇ζ_k(y) = −k(y − x)/|y − x| has length k; ∇ζ_k = 0 on the open sets {|y − x| < ρ − 1/k} and {|y − x| > ρ}; the two spheres are L^N-null. Hence
 ∫_E |∇ζ_k| = k L^N(E ∩ A_k) = k(V(ρ) − V(ρ − 1/k)) → V'(ρ), and likewise ∫_{U∖E} |∇ζ_k| = k(V_c(ρ) − V_c(ρ − 1/k)) → V_c'(ρ) (A_k ⊆ B_ρ ⊆ U).
By dominated convergence (|ζ_k⟨ν, e⟩| ≤ 1_{B̄_ρ} μ-a.e., μ(B̄_ρ) < ∞), ∫ ζ_k⟨ν, e⟩ dμ → ∫_{B_ρ} ⟨ν, e⟩ dμ. So (3) and (3c) with w = e give
 (5) ∫_{B_ρ} ⟨ν, e⟩ dμ ≤ min(V'(ρ), V_c'(ρ)) for a.e. ρ ∈ (0, ρ₀).
Moreover, for ρ' < ρ, V(ρ) − V(ρ') ≤ L^N(B_ρ ∖ B_{ρ'}) = ω_N(ρ^N − ρ'^N), so V'(ρ) ≤ Nω_N ρⁿ; likewise V_c'(ρ) ≤ Nω_N ρⁿ.

Step 5 (Simon (6) and the mass bound (6')). By Step 2 choose ρ₁ ∈ (0, ρ₀) with a(ρ) ≥ 1/2, i.e. ∫_{B_ρ} ⟨ν, e⟩ dμ ≥ m(ρ)/2, for all ρ ∈ (0, ρ₁). Then (5) gives, for a.e. ρ ∈ (0, ρ₁),
 (6) m(ρ) ≤ 2V'(ρ), m(ρ) ≤ 2V_c'(ρ), m(ρ) ≤ 2Nω_N ρⁿ.
For an arbitrary ρ ∈ (0, ρ₁) choose ρ_j ↓ ρ in (ρ, ρ₁) outside the exceptional null set; by monotonicity m(ρ) ≤ m(ρ_j) ≤ 2Nω_N ρ_jⁿ → 2Nω_N ρⁿ. Hence, with C := 2Nω_N,
 (6') μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ Cρⁿ for every ρ ∈ (0, ρ₁).
Also B_{ρ₁} ⊆ B̄_{ρ₀} ⊆ U.

Step 6 (excess decay). For ρ ∈ (0, ρ₁), by (2') and (6'):
 0 ≤ (ρⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_{B_ρ} |ν − e| dμ ≤ (ρⁿ)⁻¹ m(ρ) (2(1 − a(ρ)))^{1/2} ≤ C (2(1 − a(ρ)))^{1/2} → 0 as ρ ↓ 0 (Step 2).

Step 7 (the Sobolev step (S); Simon lines 689-705, errata E5, E6). Constants: for N ≥ 2 let c_N be the Gagliardo-Nirenberg-Sobolev constant, ‖w‖_{L^{N/(N−1)}} ≤ c_N ∫ |∇w| for w ∈ C¹_c(ℝ^N) ([GT01, Thm 7.10]; Mathlib eLpNorm_le_eLpNorm_fderiv_of_eq); for N = 1, sup|w| ≤ ½ ∫ |w'| for w ∈ C¹_c(ℝ) (w(t) = ∫_{−∞}^t w' = −∫_t^∞ w'). Both extend to Lipschitz w with compact support: apply them to φ_τ * w ∈ C^∞_c, note ∫|∇(φ_τ * w)| = ∫|φ_τ * ∇w| ≤ ∫|∇w|, and let τ → 0 (φ_τ * w → w uniformly with supports in a fixed compact set).
Let G ∈ {E, U ∖ E} with Gauss-Green pair (μ, ν_G), where ν_G := ν if G = E and ν_G := −ν if G = U ∖ E (sibling compl_pair). Let ζ ≥ 0 be Lipschitz with compact support and tsupport ζ ⊆ U. Claim:
 (S) if N ≥ 2: ‖ζχ_G‖_{L^{N/(N−1)}} ≤ c_N (∫ ζ dμ + ∫_G |∇ζ|); if N = 1: ess sup ζχ_G ≤ ½ (∫ ζ dμ + ∫_G |∇ζ|).
Proof. Fix σ₀ > 0 with K' := {y : dist(y, tsupport ζ) ≤ 2σ₀} ⊆ U. For σ ∈ (0, σ₀) let u_σ := φ_σ * χ_G (C^∞, 0 ≤ u_σ ≤ 1, ∇u_σ = (∇φ_σ) * χ_G) and w_σ := ζ u_σ (Lipschitz with compact support); then ∫|∇w_σ| ≤ ∫ ζ|∇u_σ| + ∫ u_σ|∇ζ|.
 (a) Let g : ℝ^N → ℝ^N be continuous with compact support and |g| ≤ ζ pointwise, and put g̃(z) := ∫ g(y) φ_σ(y − z) dy. Then g̃ is C^∞, tsupport g̃ ⊆ tsupport ζ + B̄_σ(0) ⊆ K' ⊆ U, |g̃| ≤ ζ̃_σ := ∫ ζ(y) φ_σ(y − ·) dy, and div g̃(z) = −∫ ⟨g(y), ∇φ_σ(y − z)⟩ dy. By Fubini, ∫ ⟨g, ∇u_σ⟩ = ∫_G ∫ ⟨g(y), ∇φ_σ(y − z)⟩ dy dz = −∫_G div g̃ = −∫_{G∩U} div g̃ = ∫ ⟨g̃, ν_G⟩ dμ ≤ ∫ ζ̃_σ dμ, by (GG) for (U, G, μ, ν_G) and |ν_G| = 1 μ-a.e. Taking g_j := ζ ∇u_σ/(|∇u_σ| + 1/j) (continuous, compact support, |g_j| ≤ ζ) and letting j → ∞ (monotone convergence) gives ∫ ζ|∇u_σ| ≤ ∫ ζ̃_σ dμ.
 (b) As σ → 0: ζ̃_σ → ζ uniformly with supports in K' and μ(K') < ∞, so ∫ ζ̃_σ dμ → ∫ ζ dμ; along a sequence σ_j → 0, u_{σ_j} → χ_G a.e. (Lebesgue differentiation theorem) with 0 ≤ u_{σ_j} ≤ 1, so ∫ u_{σ_j}|∇ζ| → ∫_G |∇ζ| and w_{σ_j} → ζχ_G a.e.
 (c) If N ≥ 2, Fatou's lemma and the Lipschitz Sobolev inequality give ‖ζχ_G‖_{N/(N−1)} ≤ liminf_j ‖w_{σ_j}‖_{N/(N−1)} ≤ c_N liminf_j ∫ |∇w_{σ_j}| ≤ c_N (∫ ζ dμ + ∫_G |∇ζ|). If N = 1, ess sup ζχ_G ≤ liminf_j sup|w_{σ_j}| ≤ ½ liminf_j ∫ |w_{σ_j}'| ≤ ½ (∫ ζ dμ + ∫_G |∇ζ|).

Step 8 (lower volume bounds (10), (11); Simon lines 706-733). Let G ∈ {E, U ∖ E} and V_G := V resp. V_c; for 0 < ρ ≤ ρ₀ we have G ∩ B_ρ = E ∩ B_ρ resp. B_ρ ∖ E, since B_ρ ⊆ U.
 (i) V_G(ρ) > 0 for every ρ ∈ (0, ρ₁). Otherwise χ_G = 0 a.e. on B_ρ. Take ρ' ∈ (0, ρ) and the cut-offs ζ_k of Step 4 built with ρ' in place of ρ. Step 3 for the pair (μ, ν_G) with w_G := e (G = E) resp. w_G := −e (G = U ∖ E), for which ⟨ν_G, w_G⟩ = ⟨ν, e⟩, gives ∫ ζ_k⟨ν, e⟩ dμ = −∫_G ⟨∇ζ_k, w_G⟩ = 0, because ∇ζ_k vanishes outside B_{ρ'} ⊆ B_ρ, where χ_G = 0 a.e. Letting k → ∞ (dominated convergence) gives ∫_{B_{ρ'}} ⟨ν, e⟩ dμ = 0, contradicting ∫_{B_{ρ'}} ⟨ν, e⟩ dμ ≥ m(ρ')/2 > 0 (Steps 1 and 5).
 (ii) Let ρ ∈ (0, ρ₁) be such that V and V_c are differentiable at ρ and (6) holds at ρ (this is a.e. ρ). Apply (S) with ζ = ζ_k from Step 4 and let k → ∞: ∫ ζ_k dμ ≤ m(ρ) (ζ_k ≤ 1_{B_ρ}); ∫_G |∇ζ_k| → V_G'(ρ); and, for N ≥ 2, ‖ζ_kχ_G‖_{N/(N−1)} ↑ V_G(ρ)^{(N−1)/N} (monotone convergence, ζ_k ↑ 1_{B_ρ}). Hence V_G(ρ)^{(N−1)/N} ≤ c_N(m(ρ) + V_G'(ρ)) ≤ 3c_N V_G'(ρ) by (6). For N = 1: since V_G(ρ) > 0 and L^1(G ∩ B_{ρ−1/k}) ↑ V_G(ρ), for large k the set G ∩ B_{ρ−1/k}, on which ζ_kχ_G = 1, has positive measure; so ess sup ζ_kχ_G = 1 and 1 ≤ ½(m(ρ) + V_G'(ρ)) ≤ (3/2)V_G'(ρ).
 (iii) Integration (Simon: "Integration (using the fact that L^{n+1}(E ∩ B_ρ(0)) is non-decreasing) then implies (10)"). If N ≥ 2, W := V_G^{1/N} is non-decreasing on [0, ρ₁], and at each ρ as in (ii) we have V_G(ρ) > 0 and V_G'(ρ) > 0, so W is differentiable at ρ with W'(ρ) = V_G'(ρ)/(N V_G(ρ)^{(N−1)/N}) ≥ 1/(3Nc_N). For 0 < ε < ρ < ρ₁, the integral of the a.e. derivative of a non-decreasing function is at most its increment (Mathlib MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc), so W(ρ) ≥ W(ρ) − W(ε) ≥ ∫_ε^ρ W' ≥ (ρ − ε)/(3Nc_N); letting ε ↓ 0, V_G(ρ) ≥ (3Nc_N)^{−N} ρ^N. If N = 1, V_G' ≥ 2/3 a.e. on (0, ρ₁), and in the same way V_G(ρ) ≥ (2/3)ρ.
 Hence, with c := (3Nc_N)^{−N} if N ≥ 2 and c := 2/3 if N = 1 (so c > 0): L^N(E ∩ B_ρ) ≥ cρ^N (10) and L^N(B_ρ ∖ E) ≥ cρ^N (11) for every ρ ∈ (0, ρ₁).

Step 9 (conclusion). ρ₁ > 0 and B_{ρ₁}(x) ⊆ U (Step 5); with C = 2Nω_N and c > 0 as above, (6'), (10) and (11) hold for every ρ ∈ (0, ρ₁) as inequalities of real numbers, hence as the stated inequalities μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(Cρⁿ), ENNReal.ofReal(cρ^{n+1}) ≤ L^N(E ∩ B_ρ(x)) and ENNReal.ofReal(cρ^{n+1}) ≤ L^N(B_ρ(x) ∖ E) (N = n + 1). Step 6 gives (ρⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_{B_ρ(x)} |ν − e| dμ → 0 as ρ ↓ 0. ∎

(GG) extends to Lipschitz fields by mollification; with the complement pair (sibling compl_pair) this gives ∫ζ⟨ν, e⟩dμ ≤ min(∫_E|∇ζ|, ∫_{U∖E}|∇ζ|) (Simon (3)).

Radial piecewise-linear cut-offs ζ_k ↑ 1_{B_ρ}: ∫_{B_ρ}⟨ν,e⟩dμ ≤ min(V'(ρ), V_c'(ρ)) for a.e. ρ (5); with a(ρ) ≥ 1/2 this gives μ(B_ρ) ≤ 2V', 2V_c', 2Nω_Nρⁿ a.e. (6), and μ(B_ρ) ≤ Cρⁿ for all ρ < ρ₁ (6').

V_G > 0 on (0, ρ₁); (S) with ζ_k gives V_G^{(N−1)/N} ≤ 3c_N V_G' a.e. (resp. V_G' ≥ 2/3 for N = 1); integrating the a.e. derivative of the monotone V_G^{1/N} yields V_G(ρ) ≥ cρ^N, i.e. (10), (11).

subproblems.title: Compactness for sets with locally uniformly bounded perimeter (Simon Ch. 2, Thm 2.6, for characteristic functions)
subproblems.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ and let (F_k)_{k∈ℕ} be Lebesgue null-measurable subsets of ℝ^N. Assume that for every R > 0 there is C_R ∈ ℝ such that for all sufficiently large k and every C¹ map g : ℝ^N → ℝ^N with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ B_R(0) and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y, ∫_{F_k} div g dL^N ≤ C_R. Then there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and a measurable G ⊆ ℝ^N such that L^N(K ∩ (F_{φ(k)} Δ G)) → 0 as k → ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^N.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (F : ℕ → Set (Rn N)), (∀ k, NullMeasurableSet (F k) volume) → (∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ k in atTop, ∀ g : Rn N → Rn N, ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ Metric.ball 0 R → (∀ y, ‖g y‖ ≤ 1) → ∫ y in F k, Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanDivergence g y ≤ C) → ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∃ G : Set (Rn N), MeasurableSet G ∧ ∀ K : Set (Rn N), IsCompact K → Tendsto (fun k ↦ volume (K ∩ symmDiff (F (φ k)) G)) atTop (𝓝 0)

Source. Parent proof Part 3b; Simon, Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 4.3, lines 653-655 ("by the Compactness Theorem 2.6 of Ch. 2, it follows that we can select a sequence ρ_k ↓ 0 so that χ_{ρ_k⁻¹E} → χ_F in L¹_loc", erratum E2: printed χ_R), and Simon, Ch. 2, Theorem 2.6 (chapter-02.txt lines 598-628), proved there by mollification and Arzelà's theorem ([GT01, Thm 7.22]). SimonGMT contains only the closure half (Chapter02/BV.lean, isLocallyBV_of_locallyL1_of_uniform_bound: "Extracting a convergent subsequence remains the compactness obligation") and Mathlib has no BV compactness, so the mollification/Arzelà-Ascoli route of the parent is written out.

Notation. L^N = volume; χ_k := 1_{F_k}; div g = euclideanDivergence g; φ ∈ C^∞_c(B_1(0)) with φ ≥ 0, ∫φ = 1, φ(−y) = φ(y), and φ_σ(y) := σ^{−N}φ(y/σ) for σ > 0.

Step 0 (N = 0). ℝ⁰ = {0}, so each F_k is ∅ or {0}. One of these two values is taken for infinitely many k; let φ enumerate those k increasingly and let G be that value (measurable). Then F_{φ(k)} Δ G = ∅ for all k, and the conclusion holds. From now on N ≥ 1.

Step 1 (reductions). Replacing each F_k by a measurable F_k' with L^N(F_k Δ F_k') = 0 changes neither the hypothesis nor the conclusion, so assume every F_k measurable. For each integer R ≥ 1 fix C_R and k_R such that the hypothesis holds for all k ≥ k_R; replacing C_R by max(C_R, 0) we may assume C_R ≥ 0. Applying the hypothesis to g and to −g (both admissible), |∫_{F_k} div g| ≤ C_R for k ≥ k_R and every admissible g.

Step 2 (translation estimate). For an integer R ≥ 1, h ∈ ℝ^N with |h| ≤ 1 and k ≥ k_{R+1}:
 ∫_{B_R(0)} |χ_k(y + h) − χ_k(y)| dy ≤ C_{R+1}|h|.
Proof. Let h ≠ 0 (h = 0 is trivial). Let ψ ∈ C¹_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) with tsupport ψ ⊆ B_R(0) and |ψ| ≤ 1. By translation invariance, ∫(χ_k(y + h) − χ_k(y))ψ(y) dy = ∫ χ_k(z)(ψ(z − h) − ψ(z)) dz. For each z, ψ(z − h) − ψ(z) = −∫_0^1 ⟨∇ψ(z − th), h⟩ dt = −∫_0^1 div Ψ_t(z) dt, where Ψ_t(z) := ψ(z − th)h. Each Ψ_t is C¹ with compact support, |Ψ_t| ≤ |h|, and tsupport Ψ_t = tsupport ψ + th ⊆ B_{R+1}(0) (tsupport ψ is a compact subset of B_R(0), hence lies in B̄_{R'}(0) for some R' < R, and |th| ≤ 1). By Fubini (bounded integrands with compact support), ∫ χ_k(ψ(· − h) − ψ) = −∫_0^1 ∫_{F_k} div Ψ_t dz dt, and Step 1 applied to Ψ_t/|h| gives |∫_{F_k} div Ψ_t| ≤ C_{R+1}|h|. Hence |∫(χ_k(· + h) − χ_k)ψ| ≤ C_{R+1}|h|. Finally let s := sgn(χ_k(· + h) − χ_k)·1_{B_R(0)}. There are ψ_j ∈ C^∞_c(ℝ^N) with tsupport ψ_j ⊆ B_R(0), |ψ_j| ≤ 1 and ψ_j → s a.e. (approximate s in L¹(B_R(0)) by continuous functions with compact support in B_R(0), truncate them to [−1, 1], mollify with radius smaller than the distance of their supports to ∂B_R(0) and less than 1/j, and pass to an a.e. convergent subsequence). Dominated convergence gives ∫_{B_R(0)} |χ_k(· + h) − χ_k| = lim_j ∫(χ_k(· + h) − χ_k)ψ_j ≤ C_{R+1}|h|.

Step 3 (mollification error). For σ ∈ (0, 1], an integer R ≥ 1 and k ≥ k_{R+1}: since (φ_σ * χ_k)(y) − χ_k(y) = ∫ φ_σ(h)(χ_k(y − h) − χ_k(y)) dh, Fubini and Step 2 (applied with −h, |h| ≤ σ ≤ 1) give
 ‖φ_σ * χ_k − χ_k‖_{L¹(B_R(0))} ≤ ∫ φ_σ(h) C_{R+1}|h| dh ≤ σ C_{R+1}.

Step 4 (equicontinuity). For fixed σ > 0 the functions v_k^σ := φ_σ * χ_k take values in [0, 1] and are Lipschitz with constant L_σ := ∫ |∇φ_σ|, uniformly in k: |v_k^σ(y) − v_k^σ(y')| ≤ ∫ |φ_σ(y − z) − φ_σ(y' − z)| dz ≤ |y − y'| ∫ |∇φ_σ|.

Step 5 (diagonal subsequence). For each integer m ≥ 1, the restrictions of (v_k^{1/m})_k to the compact ball B̄_m(0) are uniformly bounded and equi-Lipschitz, so by the Arzelà-Ascoli theorem every subsequence has a further subsequence converging uniformly on B̄_m(0). Choose inductively strictly increasing maps ψ_1 and ψ_m = ψ_{m−1} ∘ θ_m (θ_m strictly increasing) such that (v^{1/m}_{ψ_m(k)})_k converges uniformly on B̄_m(0), and put φ(k) := ψ_k(k). Then φ is strictly increasing, and for every m the sequence (φ(k))_{k≥m} is a subsequence of ψ_m, so (v^{1/m}_{φ(k)})_k converges uniformly on B̄_m(0).

Step 6 (Cauchy in L¹(B_R)). Fix an integer R ≥ 1 and ε > 0; choose an integer m ≥ R with 2C_{R+1}/m < ε/2 and put σ := 1/m ≤ 1. For k, l large (so that φ(k), φ(l) ≥ k_{R+1}), Steps 3 and 5 give
 ‖χ_{φ(k)} − χ_{φ(l)}‖_{L¹(B_R(0))} ≤ ‖χ_{φ(k)} − v^σ_{φ(k)}‖ + ‖v^σ_{φ(k)} − v^σ_{φ(l)}‖ + ‖v^σ_{φ(l)} − χ_{φ(l)}‖ ≤ 2σC_{R+1} + L^N(B_R(0)) sup_{B̄_m(0)} |v^σ_{φ(k)} − v^σ_{φ(l)}| < ε.

Step 7 (the limit is a characteristic function). By completeness of L¹(B_R(0)) for each integer R ≥ 1, and since the limits on nested balls agree a.e., there is u ∈ L¹_loc(ℝ^N) with χ_{φ(k)} → u in L¹(B_R(0)) for every R. A subsequence converges a.e. on each ball B_R(0) (diagonally, a.e. on ℝ^N), and χ_{φ(k)} takes values in {0, 1}, so u ∈ {0, 1} a.e. Fix a Borel representative ũ of u and set G := {y : ũ(y) = 1}. Then G is measurable and 1_G = u a.e.

Step 8 (conclusion). Let K be compact and choose an integer R ≥ 1 with K ⊆ B_R(0). Then L^N(K ∩ (F_{φ(k)} Δ G)) = ∫_K |χ_{φ(k)} − 1_G| ≤ ‖χ_{φ(k)} − u‖_{L¹(B_R(0))} → 0 as k → ∞. ∎
proof_key_steps: N = 0 by pigeonhole; otherwise the hypothesis applied to ±g gives |∫_{F_k} div g| ≤ C_R for k ≥ k_R.
Translation estimate ∫_{B_R}|χ_k(·+h) − χ_k| ≤ C_{R+1}|h| from ψ(z−h) − ψ(z) = −∫_0^1 div(ψ(·−th)h)(z)dt and L¹-duality.
Mollification error ‖φ_σ*χ_k − χ_k‖_{L¹(B_R)} ≤ σC_{R+1}; the φ_σ*χ_k ∈ [0,1] are equi-Lipschitz for fixed σ.
Arzelà-Ascoli on each B̄_m(0) and a diagonal argument give φ with φ_{1/m}*χ_{φ(k)} uniformly convergent on B̄_m(0) for every m.
(χ_{φ(k)}) is Cauchy in every L¹(B_R); the L¹_loc limit is {0,1}-valued, equal a.e. to 1_G with G measurable, so L^N(K ∩ (F_{φ(k)} Δ G)) → 0.

subproblems.title: Rigidity: a horizontally invariant, vertically monotone set with two-sided positive volume near 0 is the half-space {⟨y, e⟩ > 0}
subproblems.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, G ⊆ ℝ^N Lebesgue null-measurable and e ∈ ℝ^N with |e| = 1. Assume (H) ∫_G Dζ(y)v dy = 0 for every C¹ compactly supported ζ : ℝ^N → ℝ and every v ∈ ℝ^N with ⟨v, e⟩ = 0; (M) ∫_G Dζ(y)e dy ≤ 0 for every C¹ compactly supported ζ : ℝ^N → ℝ with ζ ≥ 0; (P) L^N(G ∩ B_R(0)) > 0 and L^N(B_R(0) ∖ G) > 0 for every R > 0. Then L^N(G Δ {y : ⟨y, e⟩ > 0}) = 0.

Source. Parent proof Parts 3c, 3d (with the corrected sign, erratum E1) and the end of 3e; Simon, Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 4.3, chapter-03.txt lines 656-688 (∫_F D_iζ = 0 for i = 1, ..., n, "F = ℝⁿ × H", "H is non-decreasing", (9) corrected to F = {x^{n+1} > λ}) and line 733 ("(10) and (11) evidently tell us that λ = 0"). The parent's two mollification arguments (for the horizontal derivatives in 3c, and for "the distributional derivative of χ_H is a non-negative measure, so χ_H agrees a.e. with a non-decreasing function" in 3d) are carried out together, in coordinates adapted to e.

Notation. L^N = volume; u := χ_G (bounded, locally integrable); D_vζ(y) := Dζ(y)v (Lean fderiv ℝ ζ y v); φ_σ (σ > 0) an even standard mollifier (C^∞, ≥ 0, ∫φ_σ = 1, spt φ_σ ⊆ B̄_σ(0)); u_σ := φ_σ * u.

Step 0. N ≥ 1, because |e| = 1 while ℝ⁰ = {0}.

Step 1 (mollified derivatives; Simon (7)-(8) and the vertical sign). u_σ is C^∞ with 0 ≤ u_σ ≤ 1 and, differentiating under the integral sign, D_v u_σ(y) = ∫ u(z) (D_vφ_σ)(y − z) dz for all y, v. For fixed y, ζ_y(z) := φ_σ(y − z) is C^∞ with compact support, ζ_y ≥ 0, and D_vζ_y(z) = −(D_vφ_σ)(y − z). Hence D_v u_σ(y) = −∫_G D_vζ_y(z) dz. By (H), D_v u_σ ≡ 0 for every v with ⟨v, e⟩ = 0 (horizontal invariance); by (M), D_e u_σ(y) = −∫_G D_eζ_y ≥ 0 for every y (vertical monotonicity).

Step 2 (one-variable structure; "F = ℝⁿ × H"). For y ∈ ℝ^N let π(y) := y − ⟨y, e⟩e, so ⟨π(y), e⟩ = 0. Along the segment s ↦ ⟨y, e⟩e + sπ(y), s ∈ [0, 1], the derivative of u_σ is D_{π(y)}u_σ = 0, so u_σ(y) = u_σ(⟨y, e⟩e). Thus u_σ(y) = w_σ(⟨y, e⟩) with w_σ(t) := u_σ(te), a C^∞ function with values in [0, 1] and w_σ'(t) = D_e u_σ(te) ≥ 0; so w_σ is non-decreasing.

Step 3 (limit). By the Lebesgue differentiation theorem (u ∈ L¹_loc), u_{σ_j} → u a.e. for σ_j := 1/j (Mathlib ContDiffBump.ae_convolution_tendsto_right_of_locallyIntegrable). Define w(t) := limsup_j w_{σ_j}(t) ∈ [0, 1]; as a pointwise limsup of non-decreasing functions, w is non-decreasing. For a.e. y, u(y) = lim_j w_{σ_j}(⟨y, e⟩) = w(⟨y, e⟩). Let Z := {y : u(y) ≠ w(⟨y, e⟩)}, an L^N-null set.

Step 4 (half-line; Simon (9) with the corrected inequality). Extend e to an orthonormal basis b_1, ..., b_{N−1}, b_N = e of ℝ^N and let T(z, t) := Σ_{i<N} z_i b_i + te. T is a linear isometry ℝ^{N−1} × ℝ → ℝ^N carrying L^{N−1} ⊗ L¹ to L^N (coordinate identification of ℝ^{N−1} × ℝ with ℝ^N followed by the linear isometry sending the standard basis to (b_1, ..., b_N); Mathlib LinearIsometryEquiv.measurePreserving), and ⟨T(z, t), e⟩ = t. Let Z' ⊇ Z be a Borel L^N-null set. By Fubini applied to the Borel set T⁻¹(Z'), for L¹-a.e. t the slice {z : T(z, t) ∈ Z'} is L^{N−1}-null, hence not all of ℝ^{N−1} (L^{N−1}(ℝ^{N−1}) > 0, also for N = 1); for such t pick z with T(z, t) ∉ Z' ⊇ Z, so w(t) = u(T(z, t)) ∈ {0, 1}. Thus w(t) ∈ {0, 1} for a.e. t. Let λ := sup{t ∈ ℝ : w(t) < 1/2} ∈ [−∞, +∞] (sup ∅ = −∞). By monotonicity w(t) ≥ 1/2 for t > λ and w(t) < 1/2 for t < λ; hence w = 1 a.e. on (λ, ∞) and w = 0 a.e. on (−∞, λ). Since u = w(⟨·, e⟩) off the null set Z', Fubini (via T, applied to Borel null supersets as above) gives u = 1 a.e. on {y : ⟨y, e⟩ > λ} and u = 0 a.e. on {y : ⟨y, e⟩ < λ}; for finite λ the hyperplane {⟨y, e⟩ = λ} is null. Therefore L^N(G Δ {y : ⟨y, e⟩ > λ}) = 0, with the conventions {⟨y, e⟩ > −∞} := ℝ^N and {⟨y, e⟩ > +∞} := ∅.

Step 5 (λ = 0). If λ > 0 (possibly λ = +∞), let R := min(λ, 1) > 0. Every y ∈ B_R(0) has ⟨y, e⟩ ≤ |y| < R ≤ λ, so B_R(0) ⊆ {⟨y, e⟩ < λ} and Step 4 gives L^N(G ∩ B_R(0)) = 0, contradicting (P). If λ < 0 (possibly λ = −∞), let R := min(−λ, 1) > 0; then B_R(0) ⊆ {⟨y, e⟩ > λ}, so L^N(B_R(0) ∖ G) = 0, again contradicting (P). Hence λ = 0, and L^N(G Δ {y : ⟨y, e⟩ > 0}) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Mollify u = χ_G: D_v u_σ(y) = −∫_G D_v[φ_σ(y − ·)], so D_v u_σ ≡ 0 for v ⊥ e by (H) and D_e u_σ ≥ 0 by (M).
Hence u_σ(y) = w_σ(⟨y, e⟩) with w_σ non-decreasing; along σ_j → 0, u = w(⟨·, e⟩) a.e. with w = limsup w_{σ_j} non-decreasing.
Fubini in coordinates (z, t) adapted to e: w ∈ {0, 1} a.e., so G = {⟨y, e⟩ > λ} up to a null set, λ ∈ [−∞, ∞].
(P) in the ball B_{min(|λ|,1)}(0) rules out λ > 0 and λ < 0, so λ = 0.

subproblems.title: (‡‡): at reduced-boundary points the blow-ups η_{x,r}(E) converge in L¹_loc to the half-space {⟨y, ν_E(x)⟩ > 0}
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, N := n + 1, U ⊆ ℝ^N open, E ⊆ ℝ^N Lebesgue null-measurable and (μ, ν) a Gauss-Green pair for (U, E) (IsGaussGreenPair U E μ ν). Let x ∈ ∂*E := reducedBoundary U μ ν, ν_E(x) := reducedNormal μ ν x and H := {y : ⟨y, ν_E(x)⟩ > 0}. Then for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^N, L^N(K ∩ (η_{x,r}(E) Δ H)) → 0 as r ↓ 0, where η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x) (blowUpMap).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (U E : Set (Rn (n + 1))) (μ : Measure (Rn (n + 1))) (ν : Rn (n + 1) → Rn (n + 1)), IsOpen U → NullMeasurableSet E volume → IsGaussGreenPair U E μ ν → ∀ x ∈ reducedBoundary U μ ν, ∀ K : Set (Rn (n + 1)), IsCompact K → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ ↦ volume (K ∩ symmDiff (blowUpMap x r '' E) {y | 0 < inner ℝ y (reducedNormal μ ν x)})) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof Parts 3a-3f; Simon, Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 4.3, chapter-03.txt lines 653-739: compactness, (7)-(9) with erratum E1 (the display after (8) must read ∫_{ρ_k⁻¹E} D_{n+1}ζ = −ρ_k^{−n}∫ζ_kν_{n+1}dμ_E ≤ o(1), so (9) reads F = {x^{n+1} > λ}) and erratum E2 (χ_F, printed χ_R), (10)-(11), and "Now given any sequence ρ_k ↓ 0, the argument above guarantees we can select a subsequence ρ_k' such that χ_{ρ_k'⁻¹E} → χ_{x^{n+1} > 0} in L¹_loc. Hence ... (‡‡) is established" (lines 734-739, sign corrected). The point x and e = ν_E(x) are kept general instead of normalizing to x = 0, e = e_N.

Notation. L^N = volume; e := ν_E(x) = reducedNormal μ ν x; H := {y : ⟨y, e⟩ > 0}; η_r := η_{x,r} = blowUpMap x r; E_r := η_r(E); D_vζ(y) := Dζ(y)v; div g = euclideanDivergence g.

Step 0 (e is a unit vector). As x ∈ ∂*E, normalAverage(x, ρ) → v with |v| = 1 as ρ ↓ 0; limits along the non-trivial filter 𝓝[>]0 are unique, so e = limUnder (𝓝[>]0) (normalAverage μ ν x) = v and |e| = 1.

Step 1 (constants). Sibling density_estimates gives ρ₁ > 0 with B_{ρ₁}(x) ⊆ U and C, c with c > 0 such that for every ρ ∈ (0, ρ₁): μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ Cρⁿ (replace C by max(C, 0)), L^N(E ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≥ cρ^N and L^N(B_ρ(x) ∖ E) ≥ cρ^N; and ε(ρ) := (ρⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_{B_ρ(x)} |ν − e| dμ → 0 as ρ ↓ 0.

Step 2 (estimates for the blow-ups; Simon 3a, (7)-(8)). Fix R > 0 and r ∈ (0, ρ₁/R). Since η_r⁻¹(B_R(0)) = B_{rR}(x) ⊆ B_{ρ₁}(x) ⊆ U, we have B_R(0) ⊆ η_r(U). Let g : ℝ^N → ℝ^N be C¹ with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ B_R(0). Sibling blowup_identity gives ∫_{E_r} div g = −(rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫ ⟨g(η_r(y)), ν(y)⟩ dμ(y), and the integrand vanishes unless y ∈ B_{rR}(x).
 (a) If |g| ≤ 1 everywhere, then, as |ν| = 1 μ-a.e., ∫_{E_r} div g ≤ (rⁿ)⁻¹ μ(B_{rR}(x)) ≤ (rⁿ)⁻¹ C(rR)ⁿ = CRⁿ.
 (b) For ζ ∈ C¹_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) with tsupport ζ ⊆ B_R(0) and v ∈ ℝ^N, take g := ζv (C¹, compact support, div g = D_vζ, ⟨g(η_r(y)), ν(y)⟩ = ζ(η_r(y))⟨v, ν(y)⟩): ∫_{E_r} D_vζ = −(rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫ ζ(η_r(y))⟨v, ν(y)⟩ dμ(y).
 (b1) If ⟨v, e⟩ = 0, then ⟨v, ν⟩ = ⟨v, ν − e⟩, so |∫_{E_r} D_vζ| ≤ sup|ζ|·|v|·(rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_{B_{rR}(x)} |ν − e| dμ = sup|ζ|·|v|·Rⁿ·ε(rR).
 (b2) If v = e and ζ ≥ 0, then ⟨e, ν⟩ = 1 − ⟨e, e − ν⟩ ≥ 1 − |ν − e|, so (corrected sign E1) ∫_{E_r} D_eζ = −(rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫ ζ(η_r(y))⟨e, ν(y)⟩ dμ ≤ −(rⁿ)⁻¹∫ζ(η_r(y))dμ + (rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫ ζ(η_r(y))|ν(y) − e| dμ(y) ≤ sup ζ·Rⁿ·ε(rR).
 The right-hand sides in (b1), (b2) tend to 0 as r ↓ 0, because rR ↓ 0.
 (c) η_r maps E ∩ B_{rR}(x) onto E_r ∩ B_R(0) and B_{rR}(x) ∖ E onto B_R(0) ∖ E_r (η_r is a bijection with η_r(B_{rR}(x)) = B_R(0)), and multiplies L^N by r^{−N}; hence L^N(E_r ∩ B_R(0)) = r^{−N}L^N(E ∩ B_{rR}(x)) ≥ cR^N and L^N(B_R(0) ∖ E_r) ≥ cR^N.

Step 3 (a convergent subsequence; Simon Ch. 2, 2.6). Let r_k > 0 with r_k → 0 and F_k := E_{r_k}; F_k is null-measurable, being the image of the null-measurable E under the affine homeomorphism η_{r_k}, which maps L^N-null sets to L^N-null sets and Borel sets to Borel sets. For every R > 0, Step 2(a) shows that the hypothesis of sibling indicator_compactness holds with constant CRⁿ for all k with r_k < ρ₁/R, i.e. for all large k. That sibling gives a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and a measurable G with L^N(K ∩ (F_{φ(k)} Δ G)) → 0 for every compact K.

Step 4 (properties of G). For a bounded Borel f vanishing outside a compact K: |∫_{F_{φ(k)}} f − ∫_G f| ≤ sup|f|·L^N(K ∩ (F_{φ(k)} Δ G)) → 0.
 (H) Let ζ ∈ C¹_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) and ⟨v, e⟩ = 0; choose R with tsupport ζ ⊆ B_R(0). With f := D_vζ and Step 2(b1): ∫_G D_vζ = lim_k ∫_{F_{φ(k)}} D_vζ = 0.
 (M) Let ζ ∈ C¹_c(ℝ^N, ℝ), ζ ≥ 0, tsupport ζ ⊆ B_R(0). With f := D_eζ and Step 2(b2): ∫_G D_eζ = lim_k ∫_{F_{φ(k)}} D_eζ ≤ lim_k sup ζ·Rⁿ·ε(r_{φ(k)}R) = 0.
 (P) Let R > 0 and K := B̄_R(0). Then |L^N(G ∩ B_R(0)) − L^N(F_{φ(k)} ∩ B_R(0))| ≤ L^N(K ∩ (F_{φ(k)} Δ G)) → 0 and likewise for B_R(0) ∖ G; with Step 2(c), L^N(G ∩ B_R(0)) ≥ cR^N > 0 and L^N(B_R(0) ∖ G) ≥ cR^N > 0.
 G is measurable, hence null-measurable, and |e| = 1 (Step 0).

Step 5 (identification; Simon (9)-(11) with λ = 0). Sibling halfspace_rigidity applied to (N, G, e) gives L^N(G Δ H) = 0. Since F Δ H ⊆ (F Δ G) ∪ (G Δ H), for every compact K: L^N(K ∩ (F_{φ(k)} Δ H)) ≤ L^N(K ∩ (F_{φ(k)} Δ G)) + L^N(G Δ H) → 0.

Step 6 (full limit; Simon lines 734-739). Fix a compact K and put a(r) := L^N(K ∩ (E_r Δ H)) ∈ [0, ∞]. Steps 3-5 show that every sequence r_k → 0 with r_k > 0 has a subsequence along which a → 0. The filter 𝓝[>]0 is countably generated, so a(r) → 0 as r ↓ 0: otherwise there would be ε > 0 and r_k ↓ 0 with a(r_k) ≥ ε for all k, and no subsequence of (a(r_k)) could tend to 0 (Mathlib tendsto_of_subseq_tendsto). ∎
proof_key_steps: e = ν_E(x) is a unit vector; sibling density_estimates gives ρ₁, the mass bound μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ Cρⁿ, the volume bounds cρ^N and the excess ε(ρ) → 0.

Sibling blowup_identity on B_R(0) ⊆ η_{x,r}(U) (r < ρ₁/R): ∫_{E_r} div g ≤ CRⁿ for |g| ≤ 1, |∫_{E_r}D_vζ| = O(ε(rR)) for v ⊥ e, ∫_{E_r}D_eζ ≤ O(ε(rR)) for ζ ≥ 0 (corrected sign), and L^N(E_r ∩ B_R), L^N(B_R ∖ E_r) ≥ cR^N.
Sibling indicator_compactness gives a subsequence E_{r_{φ(k)}} → G in L¹_loc.
G inherits (H), (M), (P); sibling halfspace_rigidity gives L^N(G Δ H) = 0, so E_{r_{φ(k)}} → H in L¹_loc.
Every sequence r_k ↓ 0 has such a subsequence, hence L^N(K ∩ (η_{x,r}(E) Δ H)) → 0 as r ↓ 0.

subproblems.title: (‡): μ has approximate tangent plane (span{ν_E(x)})^⊥ with multiplicity 1 at every reduced-boundary point
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, N := n + 1, U ⊆ ℝ^N open, E ⊆ ℝ^N Lebesgue null-measurable and (μ, ν) a Gauss-Green pair for (U, E) (IsGaussGreenPair U E μ ν). Let x ∈ ∂*E := reducedBoundary U μ ν and P := (span{ν_E(x)})^⊥ with ν_E(x) := reducedNormal μ ν x. Then HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n μ x P 1: finrank P = n and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ), (rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫ f(η_{x,r}(y)) dμ(y) → 1·∫_P f dHⁿ as r ↓ 0 (Hⁿ = μHE[n], η_{x,r} = blowUpMap x r).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (U E : Set (Rn (n + 1))) (μ : Measure (Rn (n + 1))) (ν : Rn (n + 1) → Rn (n + 1)), IsOpen U → NullMeasurableSet E volume → IsGaussGreenPair U E μ ν → ∀ x ∈ reducedBoundary U μ ν, HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n μ x ((Submodule.span ℝ {reducedNormal μ ν x})ᗮ) 1
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof Part 4; Simon, Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 4.3, chapter-03.txt lines 739-746 ("Then by 4.1, (1) and (2) we have μ_{ρ⁻¹E} → Hⁿ⌞{x^{n+1} = 0} as ρ ↓ 0"), with erratum E3 (the mass bound (6') is also needed to control ∫φ(1 − ν_{n+1})dμ_ρ) and the sign correction E1 for the limiting half-space.

Notation. L^N = volume; Hⁿ = μHE[n]; e := ν_E(x) = reducedNormal μ ν x; P := (span{e})^⊥; H := {y : ⟨y, e⟩ > 0}; η_r := η_{x,r} = blowUpMap x r; E_r := η_r(E); D_vφ(y) := Dφ(y)v; ω_n := Lⁿ(B_1(0)) (ω₀ = 1).

Step 0 (dimension). As x ∈ ∂*E, normalAverage(x, ρ) → v with |v| = 1; limits along the non-trivial filter 𝓝[>]0 are unique, so e = limUnder(...) = v and |e| = 1. Hence span{e} is a line and finrank P = (n + 1) − 1 = n (Mathlib Submodule.finrank_orthogonal_span_singleton).

Step 1 (flat facts). Choose an orthonormal basis b_1, ..., b_n of P; with b_{n+1} := e it is an orthonormal basis of ℝ^N. T(z, t) := Σ_{i≤n} z_i b_i + te is a linear isometry ℝⁿ × ℝ → ℝ^N (Euclidean norms) carrying Lⁿ ⊗ L¹ to L^N (T is the measure-preserving coordinate identification of ℝⁿ × ℝ with ℝ^{n+1} followed by the linear isometry of ℝ^N sending the standard basis to (b_1, ..., b_n, e), and linear isometries preserve Lebesgue measure: Mathlib LinearIsometryEquiv.measurePreserving), and ι(z) := T(z, 0) is an isometry of ℝⁿ onto P. Since Hausdorff measure is invariant under isometries and μHE[n] = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (Mathlib Isometry.hausdorffMeasure_image, IsometryEquiv.measurePreserving_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), Hⁿ⌞P is the image of Lⁿ under ι: ∫_P f dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝⁿ} f(ι(z)) dz for bounded Borel f with compact support, and Hⁿ(P ∩ B_R(0)) = ω_nRⁿ < ∞. (For n = 0, P = {0} and H⁰⌞P is the unit mass at 0.)
 For φ ∈ C¹_c(ℝ^N, ℝ): since (d/dt)φ(T(z, t)) = D_eφ(T(z, t)), Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus (φ has compact support) give
 ∫_H D_eφ dL^N = ∫_{ℝⁿ} ∫_0^∞ (d/dt)φ(T(z, t)) dt dz = ∫_{ℝⁿ} (−φ(T(z, 0))) dz = −∫_P φ dHⁿ.

Step 2 (constants). Sibling density_estimates gives ρ₁ > 0 with B_{ρ₁}(x) ⊆ U and C (replace C by max(C, 0)) with μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ Cρⁿ for every ρ ∈ (0, ρ₁), and ε(ρ) := (ρⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_{B_ρ(x)} |ν − e| dμ → 0 as ρ ↓ 0.

Step 3 (C¹ test functions; parent Part 4 (i)-(ii)). Let φ ∈ C¹_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) with tsupport φ ⊆ B_R(0) for some R > 0, and r ∈ (0, ρ₁/R). Then η_r⁻¹(B_R(0)) = B_{rR}(x) ⊆ U, so B_R(0) ⊆ η_r(U), and sibling blowup_identity with g := φe (C¹, compact support; div g = D_eφ; ⟨g(η_r(y)), ν(y)⟩ = φ(η_r(y))⟨e, ν(y)⟩) gives
 (rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫ φ(η_r(y))⟨e, ν(y)⟩ dμ(y) = −∫_{E_r} D_eφ.
 (i) By sibling blowup_halfspace with the compact set K := tsupport φ: |∫_{E_r} D_eφ − ∫_H D_eφ| ≤ sup|D_eφ|·L^N(K ∩ (E_r Δ H)) → 0, so by Step 1 the left side tends to −∫_H D_eφ = ∫_P φ dHⁿ as r ↓ 0.
 (ii) Since |1 − ⟨e, ν⟩| = |⟨e, e − ν⟩| ≤ |ν − e| and φ∘η_r vanishes outside B_{rR}(x): |(rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫ φ(η_r(y))(1 − ⟨e, ν(y)⟩) dμ(y)| ≤ sup|φ|·(rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫_{B_{rR}(x)} |ν − e| dμ = sup|φ|·Rⁿ·ε(rR) → 0.
 All integrals here are finite (bounded integrands supported in B_{rR}(x), μ(B_{rR}(x)) < ∞). Adding (i) and (ii): (rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫ φ(η_r(y)) dμ(y) → ∫_P φ dHⁿ as r ↓ 0.

Step 4 (continuous test functions; parent Part 4 (iii)). Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) and choose R > 1 with tsupport f ⊆ B_{R−1}(0). Given δ > 0, mollifying f with radius < 1 gives φ ∈ C^∞_c with tsupport φ ⊆ B_R(0) and sup|f − φ| ≤ δ (f is uniformly continuous). For r ∈ (0, ρ₁/R): |(rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫ (f − φ)(η_r(y)) dμ(y)| ≤ δ(rⁿ)⁻¹μ(B_{rR}(x)) ≤ δCRⁿ, and |∫_P f dHⁿ − ∫_P φ dHⁿ| ≤ δHⁿ(P ∩ B_R(0)) = δω_nRⁿ. With Step 3 for φ: limsup_{r↓0} |(rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫ f(η_r(y)) dμ(y) − ∫_P f dHⁿ| ≤ δ(C + ω_n)Rⁿ. As δ > 0 is arbitrary, (rⁿ)⁻¹ ∫ f(η_r(y)) dμ(y) → ∫_P f dHⁿ = 1·∫_P f dHⁿ.

Step 5 (conclusion). finrank P = n (Step 0) and the convergence of Step 4 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) are exactly HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n μ x ((span{ν_E(x)})^⊥) 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: |e| = 1 for e = ν_E(x), so finrank (span{e})^⊥ = n; via an isometry T : ℝⁿ × ℝ → ℝ^N, −∫_H D_eφ = ∫_P φ dHⁿ and Hⁿ(P ∩ B_R(0)) = ω_nRⁿ.
Sibling blowup_identity with g = φe: (rⁿ)⁻¹∫φ(η_r(y))⟨e, ν⟩dμ = −∫_{E_r}D_eφ → −∫_H D_eφ = ∫_Pφ dHⁿ by sibling blowup_halfspace.
The defect (rⁿ)⁻¹∫φ(η_r(y))(1 − ⟨e, ν⟩)dμ is at most sup|φ|Rⁿε(rR) → 0 by sibling density_estimates.
Uniform approximation of f ∈ C_c by C¹ functions, using μ(B_{rR}(x)) ≤ C(rR)ⁿ and Hⁿ(P ∩ B_R) = ω_nRⁿ, gives the limit for every f ∈ C_c.

subproblems.title: The reduced boundary is a Borel set (parent Part 5b)
subproblems.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N open, μ a Borel measure on ℝ^N with μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = 0 and μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and ν : ℝ^N → ℝ^N μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ν| = 1 μ-a.e. Then reducedBoundary U μ ν = {x ∈ U : normalAverage μ ν x ρ = μ(B_ρ(x)).toReal⁻¹ • ∫_{B_ρ(x)} ν dμ converges as ρ ↓ 0 to a vector of length 1} is a measurable (Borel) subset of ℝ^N.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (U : Set (Rn N)) (μ : Measure (Rn N)) (ν : Rn N → Rn N), IsOpen U → μ Uᶜ = 0 → (∀ K : Set (Rn N), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → AEStronglyMeasurable ν μ → (∀ᵐ y ∂μ, ‖ν y‖ = 1) → MeasurableSet (reducedBoundary U μ ν)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof Part 5b (needed so that Hⁿ⌞∂*E is a restriction to a Borel set); this is the argument Simon uses for Borel measurability of densities, Ch. 1, §3, chapter-01.txt lines 575-592 (semicontinuity in the centre and monotone dependence on the radius reduce the limit to countably many radii).

Notation. B_ρ(x) open ball; a_x(ρ) := normalAverage μ ν x ρ = μ(B_ρ(x)).toReal⁻¹ • ∫_{B_ρ(x)} ν dμ; ∂* := reducedBoundary U μ ν ⊆ U.

Step 1 (σ-finiteness). U is the increasing union of the compact sets K_i := {y : |y| ≤ i, infEdist(y, Uᶜ) ≥ 1/i} ⊆ U (i ≥ 1; Uᶜ is closed, and infEdist(y, ∅) = ∞); μ(K_i) < ∞ and μ(Uᶜ) = 0, so μ is σ-finite, in particular s-finite.

Step 2 (a measurable version of ν). Choose a strongly measurable ν̃ with ν̃ = ν μ-a.e. Then ∫_B ν dμ = ∫_B ν̃ dμ for every Borel B, so a_x(ρ) is the same for ν and ν̃ and ∂* = reducedBoundary U μ ν̃; also |ν̃| = 1 μ-a.e.

Step 3 (measurability in x for fixed ρ). The set D_ρ := {(x, y) : dist(x, y) < ρ} is open in ℝ^N × ℝ^N, hence measurable for the product σ-algebra (ℝ^N is second countable). By Step 1 and the measurability part of Fubini-Tonelli (Mathlib measurable_measure_prodMk_left, MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable.integral_prod_right), x ↦ μ(B_ρ(x)) = μ({y : (x, y) ∈ D_ρ}) is measurable, and x ↦ ∫_{B_ρ(x)} ν̃ dμ = ∫ 1_{D_ρ}(x, y)ν̃(y) dμ(y) is strongly measurable (this is the Bochner integral, equal to 0 when the integrand is not integrable, consistently with the definition of normalAverage). Hence x ↦ a_x(ρ) is measurable for each fixed ρ.

Step 4 (left continuity in ρ). Let x ∈ U and choose ρ_x > 0 with B̄_{ρ_x}(x) ⊆ U, so μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ μ(B̄_{ρ_x}(x)) < ∞ for ρ ≤ ρ_x. Let ρ ∈ (0, ρ_x] and ρ' ↑ ρ. Then B_{ρ'}(x) ↑ B_ρ(x), so μ(B_{ρ'}(x)) → μ(B_ρ(x)) (continuity from below) and ∫_{B_{ρ'}(x)} ν̃ dμ → ∫_{B_ρ(x)} ν̃ dμ (dominated convergence: |ν̃| ≤ 1 a.e., finite measure). If μ(B_ρ(x)) > 0, the map t ↦ t⁻¹ is continuous at μ(B_ρ(x)).toReal > 0, so a_x(ρ') → a_x(ρ). If μ(B_ρ(x)) = 0, then μ(B_{ρ'}(x)) = 0 and a_x(ρ') = 0 = a_x(ρ) for all ρ' ≤ ρ. So ρ ↦ a_x(ρ) is left-continuous on (0, ρ_x].

Step 5 (countable characterization). For x ∈ U the following are equivalent:
 (A) there is v with |v| = 1 and a_x(ρ) → v as ρ ↓ 0;
 (B) for every integer m ≥ 1 there is an integer j ≥ 1 with |a_x(q) − a_x(q')| ≤ 1/m for all rationals q, q' ∈ (0, 1/j), and the limit L(x) := lim_{j→∞} a_x(1/j) (which exists under the preceding Cauchy condition) satisfies |L(x)| = 1.
 (A) ⇒ (B): convergence implies the Cauchy condition along rationals, and L(x) = v. (B) ⇒ (A): given m, take j from (B), enlarged so that 1/j ≤ ρ_x (the condition persists for larger j). For real ρ, ρ' ∈ (0, 1/j) choose rationals q_i ↑ ρ and q_i' ↑ ρ' in (0, 1/j); by Step 4, |a_x(ρ) − a_x(ρ')| = lim_i |a_x(q_i) − a_x(q_i')| ≤ 1/m. Thus a_x satisfies the Cauchy criterion as ρ ↓ 0 in the complete space ℝ^N and converges to some v; necessarily v = lim_j a_x(1/j) = L(x), so |v| = 1.

Step 6 (measurability). Let C := ⋂_{m≥1} ⋃_{j≥1} ⋂_{q, q' ∈ ℚ ∩ (0, 1/j)} {x : |a_x(q) − a_x(q')| ≤ 1/m}, a countable combination of measurable sets (Step 3). Put L(x) := limUnder atTop (j ↦ a_x(1/(j+1))); as a limit of measurable functions it is measurable (Mathlib StronglyMeasurable.limUnder, measurableSet_exists_tendsto), and on C it equals the limit in (B). By Step 5 (∂* ⊆ U by definition), ∂* = U ∩ C ∩ {x : |L(x)| = 1}, an intersection of an open set and two measurable sets. Hence reducedBoundary U μ ν is measurable. ∎
proof_key_steps: μ is σ-finite (μ(Uᶜ) = 0, U σ-compact); replacing ν by a strongly measurable version does not change normalAverage or the reduced boundary.
For fixed ρ, x ↦ μ(B_ρ(x)) and x ↦ ∫_{B_ρ(x)}ν dμ are measurable (product measurability of {dist < ρ}), so x ↦ normalAverage(x, ρ) is measurable.
For x ∈ U, ρ ↦ normalAverage(x, ρ) is left-continuous on (0, ρ_x] (continuity from below and dominated convergence).
Hence x ∈ ∂*E iff x ∈ U, the Cauchy condition holds along rational radii and |lim_j normalAverage(x, 1/j)| = 1, a countable measurable description.

subproblems.title: μ is carried by the reduced boundary: μ(ℝ^N ∖ ∂*E) = 0 (Simon line 584; Lebesgue-Besicovitch differentiation)
subproblems.statement: Let N ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N open, μ a Borel measure on ℝ^N with μ(ℝ^N ∖ U) = 0 and μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and ν : ℝ^N → ℝ^N μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ν| = 1 μ-a.e. Then μ(ℝ^N ∖ reducedBoundary U μ ν) = 0, where reducedBoundary U μ ν = {x ∈ U : μ(B_ρ(x)).toReal⁻¹ • ∫_{B_ρ(x)} ν dμ converges as ρ ↓ 0 to a vector of length 1}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (N : ℕ) (U : Set (Rn N)) (μ : Measure (Rn N)) (ν : Rn N → Rn N), IsOpen U → μ Uᶜ = 0 → (∀ K : Set (Rn N), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → AEStronglyMeasurable ν μ → (∀ᵐ y ∂μ, ‖ν y‖ = 1) → μ (reducedBoundary U μ ν)ᶜ = 0

Source. Parent proof Part 5a; Simon, Ch. 3, chapter-03.txt line 584 ("Since |ν| = 1 μ_E-a.e. in U, by virtue of Theorem 3.23 of Ch. 1 we have μ_E(U ∖ ∂*E) = 0"), i.e. the Lebesgue-Besicovitch differentiation theorem for Radon measures on ℝ^N (Simon Ch. 1, Corollary 3.17 / Theorem 3.23, via the Besicovitch covering lemma; Mathlib Besicovitch.vitaliFamily, Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt, VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average).

Notation. B_ρ(y) open ball, B̄_r(y) closed ball; ⨍_A f dλ := λ(A).toReal⁻¹ • ∫_A f dλ; then normalAverage μ ν y ρ = ⨍_{B_ρ(y)} ν dμ. The argument is uniform in N (for N = 0 it also applies verbatim).

Step 1 (localization). For integers i ≥ 1 let W_i := {y : |y| < i, infEdist(y, Uᶜ) > 1/i} (with infEdist(y, ∅) = ∞). W_i is open; its closure lies in the compact set {|y| ≤ i, infEdist(y, Uᶜ) ≥ 1/i}, which is contained in U because Uᶜ is closed; and ⋃_i W_i = U. Let μ_i := μ.restrict W_i: a finite Borel measure on ℝ^N (μ(W_i) ≤ μ(closure W_i) < ∞), hence locally finite.

Step 2 (Lebesgue-Besicovitch differentiation). ν is μ_i-a.e. strongly measurable and |ν| ≤ 1 μ_i-a.e., so ν ∈ L¹(μ_i). By the Besicovitch differentiation theorem on ℝ^N, applied to the Vitali family of closed balls of μ_i (VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average for Besicovitch.vitaliFamily μ_i, together with Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt), for μ_i-a.e. y: ⨍_{B̄_r(y)} ν dμ_i → ν(y) as r ↓ 0. Choose a measurable μ_i-null set containing the exceptional points; its intersection with W_i, together with the μ-null set {y : |ν(y)| ≠ 1}, is a μ-null set Z_i such that every y ∈ W_i ∖ Z_i satisfies this convergence and |ν(y)| = 1.

Step 3 (from closed to open balls). Fix y ∈ W_i ∖ Z_i and δ₀ > 0 with B̄_{δ₀}(y) ⊆ W_i. For r ≤ δ₀, μ_i and μ agree on subsets of B̄_r(y), so ⨍_{B̄_r(y)} ν dμ → ν(y) as r ↓ 0. Given ε ∈ (0, 1), choose δ ∈ (0, δ₀] with |⨍_{B̄_r(y)} ν dμ − ν(y)| ≤ ε for r ∈ (0, δ). Since |ν(y)| = 1 > ε, these averages are nonzero, hence μ(B̄_r(y)) > 0 for r ∈ (0, δ) (if μ(B̄_r(y)) = 0 the average is 0). Let ρ ∈ (0, δ). As r ↑ ρ, B̄_r(y) ↑ B_ρ(y) (the open ball is the increasing union of the smaller closed balls), so μ(B̄_r(y)) → μ(B_ρ(y)) ∈ (0, ∞) and ∫_{B̄_r(y)} ν dμ → ∫_{B_ρ(y)} ν dμ (dominated convergence; finite measure). Hence normalAverage μ ν y ρ = ⨍_{B_ρ(y)} ν dμ = lim_{r↑ρ} ⨍_{B̄_r(y)} ν dμ, and |normalAverage μ ν y ρ − ν(y)| ≤ ε. Therefore normalAverage μ ν y ρ → ν(y) as ρ ↓ 0, with |ν(y)| = 1 and y ∈ W_i ⊆ U; that is, y ∈ reducedBoundary U μ ν.

Step 4 (conclusion). By Step 3, ℝ^N ∖ reducedBoundary U μ ν ⊆ Uᶜ ∪ ⋃_i Z_i. Since μ(Uᶜ) = 0 and μ(Z_i) = 0, countable subadditivity (of the outer measure; no measurability of the reduced boundary is needed) gives μ(ℝ^N ∖ reducedBoundary U μ ν) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Exhaust U by open sets W_i with compact closure in U; μ⌞W_i is a finite measure and ν ∈ L¹(μ⌞W_i).
Besicovitch-Lebesgue differentiation: for μ-a.e. y ∈ W_i, closed-ball averages of ν converge to ν(y), and |ν(y)| = 1.
Open-ball averages are limits of closed-ball averages of smaller radii (with μ(B̄_r(y)) > 0), so normalAverage(y, ρ) → ν(y), a unit vector: y ∈ ∂*E.
Countable union of the μ-null exceptional sets together with μ(Uᶜ) = 0.

subproblems.title: A locally finite measure with unit-multiplicity tangent planes at every point of a carrying Borel set S: S is rectifiable and μ = Hⁿ⌞S (parent Parts 5c-5d)
subproblems.statement: Assume (RT) [the frozen type of root.rectifiable_of_tangent_measure-a1]: for all n, ℓ ∈ ℕ and every Borel measure λ on ℝ^{n+ℓ} with λ(K) < ∞ for every compact K such that for λ-a.e. y there are a subspace P and θ > 0 with HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n λ y P θ, there is a measurable, countably n-rectifiable R ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ} with λ(ℝ^{n+ℓ} ∖ R) = 0; and (AT) ApproximateTangentCharacterization (Simon Ch. 3, Theorem 1.6). Then for all n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^{n+ℓ}, every measurable S ⊆ U and every Borel measure μ on ℝ^{n+ℓ} with μ(ℝ^{n+ℓ} ∖ U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, μ(ℝ^{n+ℓ} ∖ S) = 0, and such that for every x ∈ S there is a subspace P with HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n μ x P 1: S is countably n-rectifiable and μ = Hⁿ⌞S (μ = μHE[n].restrict S).
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Rn (n + ℓ))), (∀ K : Set (Rn (n + ℓ)), IsCompact K → μ K < ∞) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∃ (P : Submodule ℝ (Rn (n + ℓ))) (θ : ℝ), 0 < θ ∧ HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n μ x P θ) → ∃ R : Set (Rn (n + ℓ)), MeasurableSet R ∧ CountablyRectifiable n R ∧ μ Rᶜ = 0) → ApproximateTangentCharacterization → ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (U S : Set (Rn (n + ℓ))) (μ : Measure (Rn (n + ℓ))), IsOpen U → μ Uᶜ = 0 → (∀ K : Set (Rn (n + ℓ)), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → MeasurableSet S → S ⊆ U → μ Sᶜ = 0 → (∀ x ∈ S, ∃ P : Submodule ℝ (Rn (n + ℓ)), HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n μ x P 1) → CountablyRectifiable n S ∧ μ = (μHE[n] : Measure (Rn (n + ℓ))).restrict S
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof Parts 5c and 5d, with erratum E4: Simon, Ch. 3, chapter-03.txt line 604 ("By 1.6 and 3.6 of Ch. 1, the first part of the theorem follows from (‡)") is only a sketch, because Theorem 1.6 concerns Hⁿ⌞M rather than μ_E; the measure form of 1.6 "⇐" (hypothesis (RT)) and density comparison are used instead. Ingredients: Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.3 (chapter-01.txt lines 602-610; SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_3), Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3) (density 1 from an approximate tangent plane), and the Besicovitch-Radon-Nikodym differentiation theorem (Simon Ch. 1, Theorems 3.22-3.24; Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv). In the parent the hypotheses are discharged by Submission.rectifiable_of_approx_tangent_measure and Submission.approximateTangentCharacterizations_hold.1, and the theorem is applied with ℓ = 1 and S = ∂*E.

Notation. N := n + ℓ; Hⁿ := μHE[n], which coincides with Simon's normalized Hausdorff measure Hⁿ(A) = lim_{δ↓0} inf{Σ_j ω_n(diam C_j/2)ⁿ : A ⊆ ⋃_j C_j, diam C_j < δ} (SimonGMT simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure; for n = 0 the term (diam C/2)⁰ is 1); ω_n := Lⁿ(B_1(0)) (ω₀ = 1); B_ρ(x) open, B̄_ρ(x) closed ball; η_{x,r} = blowUpMap x r. For x ∈ S fix P_x with HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n μ x P_x 1 (so finrank P_x = n).

Step 1 (n-planes). For an n-dimensional subspace P ⊆ ℝ^N there is a linear isometry ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N with range P. Hausdorff measure is invariant under isometries and μHE[n] = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, Isometry.hausdorffMeasure_image), so Hⁿ⌞P is the image of Lⁿ under ι; in particular Hⁿ(P ∩ B_s(0)) = Hⁿ(P ∩ B̄_s(0)) = ω_n sⁿ for s > 0 (for n = 0, P = {0} and H⁰⌞P is the unit mass at 0).

Step 2 (localization). For integers i ≥ 1 let W_i := {y : |y| < i, infEdist(y, Uᶜ) > 1/i} (infEdist(y, ∅) = ∞). The W_i are open and increasing, closure(W_i) is compact and contained in U, ⋃_i W_i = U, and μ(closure W_i) < ∞.

Step 3 (density of μ on S). For every x ∈ S: μ(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) → 1 and μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) → 1 as ρ ↓ 0. Proof: for τ ∈ (0, 1/2) let f_τ, g_τ ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, [0, 1]) be the radial piecewise-linear functions with f_τ = 1 on B̄_1(0), f_τ = 0 outside B_{1+τ}(0), g_τ = 1 on B̄_{1−τ}(0), g_τ = 0 outside B_1(0). Then g_τ∘η_{x,ρ} ≤ 1_{B_ρ(x)} ≤ 1_{B̄_ρ(x)} ≤ f_τ∘η_{x,ρ}, hence (ρⁿ)⁻¹∫ g_τ(η_{x,ρ}(y)) dμ ≤ (ρⁿ)⁻¹μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ (ρⁿ)⁻¹μ(B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ (ρⁿ)⁻¹∫ f_τ(η_{x,ρ}(y)) dμ, all finite for ρ small (B̄_{2ρ}(x) ⊆ U). By HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n μ x P_x 1 the outer terms converge to ∫_{P_x} g_τ dHⁿ ≥ Hⁿ(P_x ∩ B̄_{1−τ}(0)) = ω_n(1−τ)ⁿ and ∫_{P_x} f_τ dHⁿ ≤ Hⁿ(P_x ∩ B_{1+τ}(0)) = ω_n(1+τ)ⁿ (Step 1). Let τ ↓ 0.

Step 4 (D1: Hⁿ ≤ μ on S). For every Borel A ⊆ S, Hⁿ(A) ≤ μ(A). Proof: let O be open with A ⊆ O ⊆ U. For x ∈ A we have B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ O for small ρ, so by Step 3 the upper density limsup_{ρ↓0} μ(O ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) equals 1. Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.3 (μ is Borel regular; t = 1, A₁ := A ⊆ A₂ := O; in SimonGMT, simon_theorem_3_3 with dimensionalUpperDensity μ n O x ≥ 1, whose quotient is μ(O ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ)) gives Hⁿ(A) ≤ μ(O). Outer regularity: given ε > 0 and W_0 := ∅, apply outer regularity of the finite Borel measure μ⌞W_i on ℝ^N to the Borel set A ∩ (W_i ∖ W_{i−1}) and intersect with W_i, obtaining an open O_i ⊆ W_i containing A ∩ (W_i ∖ W_{i−1}) with μ(O_i) ≤ μ(A ∩ (W_i ∖ W_{i−1})) + ε2^{−i}. Then O := ⋃_i O_i is open, A ⊆ O ⊆ U and μ(O) ≤ μ(A) + ε. Hence Hⁿ(A) ≤ μ(A).

Step 5 (rectifiability of S; parent 5c). Fix i and let μ_i := μ.restrict W_i, a finite measure, so μ_i(K) < ∞ for every compact K. For x ∈ S ∩ W_i and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) with tsupport f ⊆ B_R(0), f∘η_{x,r} vanishes outside B_{rR}(x) ⊆ W_i for small r, so ∫ f(η_{x,r}(y)) dμ_i = ∫ f(η_{x,r}(y)) dμ and HasApproxTangentPlaneWithMultiplicity n μ_i x P_x 1 holds. Since μ_i(ℝ^N ∖ (S ∩ W_i)) ≤ μ(Sᶜ) + μ_i(W_iᶜ) = 0, this holds for μ_i-a.e. x, with θ = 1 > 0. By (RT) there is a measurable countably n-rectifiable R_i with μ_i(R_iᶜ) = 0. R := ⋃_i R_i is measurable and countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_iUnion), and μ(U ∖ R) ≤ Σ_i μ(W_i ∖ R_i) = Σ_i μ_i(R_iᶜ) = 0. Now S ∖ R is a Borel subset of S with μ(S ∖ R) = 0, so Hⁿ(S ∖ R) = 0 by Step 4. If R ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and F_j Lipschitz (Definition 1.1), then S ⊆ ((S ∖ R) ∪ M₀) ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ((S ∖ R) ∪ M₀) = 0; so S is countably n-rectifiable.

Step 6 (D2: μ ≤ 2ⁿHⁿ on S). For every Borel A ⊆ S, μ(A) ≤ 2ⁿHⁿ(A). Proof: fix τ > 0 and for integers j ≥ 1 let A_j := {x ∈ A : μ(B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ (1 + τ)ω_nρⁿ for all ρ ∈ (0, 1/j)}; by Step 3, A_j ↑ A. Let (C_m) be any countable cover of A_j by sets with diam C_m < 1/j; discard those not meeting A_j, pick x_m ∈ C_m ∩ A_j and put d_m := diam C_m, so C_m ⊆ B̄_{d_m}(x_m). If d_m > 0 then μ(C_m ∩ A_j) ≤ μ(B̄_{d_m}(x_m)) ≤ (1 + τ)ω_n d_mⁿ = 2ⁿ(1 + τ)ω_n(d_m/2)ⁿ. If d_m = 0 then C_m = {x_m} and μ({x_m}) ≤ inf_{0<ρ<1/j} (1 + τ)ω_nρⁿ, which is 0 if n ≥ 1 and ≤ 1 + τ = 2⁰(1 + τ)ω₀(d_m/2)⁰ if n = 0. Summing over m, μ(A_j) ≤ 2ⁿ(1 + τ) Σ_m ω_n(d_m/2)ⁿ; taking the infimum over such covers, μ(A_j) ≤ 2ⁿ(1 + τ) Hⁿ_{1/j}(A_j) ≤ 2ⁿ(1 + τ)Hⁿ(A). Let j → ∞ (μ(A_j) → μ(A) along the increasing sequence A_j ↑ A, valid without measurability of the A_j: Mathlib tendsto_measure_iUnion_atTop) and then τ ↓ 0.

Step 7 (density of Hⁿ⌞S). For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ S: Hⁿ(S ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) → 1 as ρ ↓ 0. Proof: fix i and M_i := S ∩ W_i. M_i is measurable (hence Hⁿ-null-measurable), countably n-rectifiable (a subset of S; Step 5), and Hⁿ(M_i ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(M_i) ≤ μ(M_i) ≤ μ(closure W_i) < ∞ for every compact K (Step 4). By (AT), direction "⇒" (with this n, ℓ), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_i there is P with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_i x P (Simon Def. 1.4: finrank P = n and ∫_{η_{x,r}(M_i)} f dHⁿ → ∫_P f dHⁿ for every f ∈ C_c). For such x, with f_τ, g_τ as in Step 3: since η_{x,r} is a translation followed by a homothety of ratio r⁻¹, Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(B)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(B) (Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image and isometry invariance), so (rⁿ)⁻¹Hⁿ(M_i ∩ B̄_r(x)) = Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(M_i) ∩ B̄_1(0)) lies between ∫_{η_{x,r}(M_i)} g_τ dHⁿ and ∫_{η_{x,r}(M_i)} f_τ dHⁿ, whose limits lie in [ω_n(1−τ)ⁿ, ω_n(1+τ)ⁿ] by Step 1; let τ ↓ 0 (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3)). For x ∈ W_i and small ρ, M_i ∩ B̄_ρ(x) = S ∩ B̄_ρ(x). Since S = ⋃_i M_i, the claim follows.

Step 8 (equality; parent 5d). Let σ := Hⁿ⌞S = μHE[n].restrict S. Fix i, and let ν_i := μ.restrict W_i and σ_i := σ.restrict W_i. Both are finite Borel measures on ℝ^N (σ_i(ℝ^N) = Hⁿ(S ∩ W_i) ≤ μ(S ∩ W_i) < ∞ by Step 4), hence locally finite; and ν_i ≪ σ_i: if B is Borel with σ_i(B) = Hⁿ(B ∩ S ∩ W_i) = 0 then ν_i(B) = μ(B ∩ W_i ∩ S) ≤ 2ⁿHⁿ(B ∩ S ∩ W_i) = 0 by μ(Sᶜ) = 0 and Step 6. By the Besicovitch differentiation theorem (Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv), for σ_i-a.e. x, ν_i(B̄_ρ(x))/σ_i(B̄_ρ(x)) → (dν_i/dσ_i)(x) as ρ ↓ 0. For σ_i-a.e. x we moreover have x ∈ S ∩ W_i and the conclusion of Step 7 at x; for such x and ρ small (B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ W_i) the ratio equals [μ(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ)] / [Hⁿ(S ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ)] → 1/1 = 1 by Steps 3 and 7. Hence dν_i/dσ_i = 1 σ_i-a.e., and since ν_i ≪ σ_i, ν_i = (dν_i/dσ_i)·σ_i = σ_i (Mathlib Measure.withDensity_rnDeriv_eq). Thus μ(B ∩ W_i) = Hⁿ(B ∩ S ∩ W_i) for every Borel B and every i. Letting i → ∞ (W_i ↑ U, S ⊆ U, μ(Uᶜ) = 0): μ(B) = μ(B ∩ U) = Hⁿ(B ∩ S ∩ U) = Hⁿ(B ∩ S) = (μHE[n].restrict S)(B) for every Borel B, so μ = μHE[n].restrict S as measures on ℝ^N.

Step 9 (conclusion). Step 5 gives CountablyRectifiable n S and Step 8 gives μ = μHE[n].restrict S. ∎
proof_key_steps: At every x ∈ S, μ(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) → 1 and μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) → 1 (squeeze with radial test functions; Hⁿ(P ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_nsⁿ).
Density comparison (Simon Ch. 1, Thm 3.3, plus outer regularity on U): Hⁿ(A) ≤ μ(A) for Borel A ⊆ S.
Localize to μ⌞W_i, apply (RT) and take the union: μ is carried by a rectifiable Borel R; Hⁿ(S ∖ R) ≤ μ(S ∖ R) = 0, so S is countably n-rectifiable.
Covering argument: μ(A) ≤ 2ⁿHⁿ(A) for Borel A ⊆ S, hence μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞S.
(AT) '⇒' on M_i = S ∩ W_i gives approximate tangent spaces Hⁿ-a.e., hence Hⁿ⌞S has density 1 at Hⁿ-a.e. point of S.
Besicovitch Radon-Nikodym differentiation of μ⌞W_i with respect to Hⁿ⌞(S ∩ W_i): the derivative is 1/1 = 1, so μ = Hⁿ⌞S.
